blocks.text: Note in passing that not only the Hebrews but also the most learned of our own scholars labour to reconcile the words חולד choled and חלד cheled, of which the former means, as they would have it, weasel, the latter earth or age, and to show how it came about that the senses of such different words were derived from one origin. There are some who understand by the word חלד cheled nothing but a short time, so that the weasel would hence be called חולד choled as a βραχύβιον [brachybion] animal. So Mercerus. For others חלד is a verb meaning to pass away gradually and to creep in; and accordingly, as they would have it, not only is the weasel called חולד choled from its stealthy movement, but time too is called חלד cheled, because it runs by silently and its motion is not perceived.
The times glide by, and we grow old with the silent years.

This is the opinion of Schindler. But for Fuller, just as חלד chalad is a verb meaning καταδῦναι [katadynai], that is, to penetrate into deep places, so the weasel is called חולד choled as a ζῶον καταδυτικὸν [zōon katadytikon], and both the earth itself and the time during which we live on earth are called חלד cheled, as it were κατάδυσις [katadysis], as Aquila renders it, that is, a hiding-place or a submersion: because here all things are full of thick darkness and are not to be compared with the light of supercelestial things. These things are indeed attractively said, but with too little solidity, as I at least think. For it is certain that the verb חלד chalad has two very different meanings, of which one prevailed among the Syrians, the other among the Arabs. For the Syrians, namely, ܚܠܕ chalad properly means to dig deep places and to penetrate, as was amply proved above. But for the Arabs خلد [khalada] chalada means something quite different, namely to remain, to endure, to last for ever, to be eternal. And just as from the former meaning came חולד [II, 447] choled for the mole, so from the latter came חלד cheled, which first means duration, as in Ps. XXXIX, 6. וחלדי, And my duration is as nothing before thee; and Ps. LXXXIX, 48. זכור אני מה חלד, Remember of what duration I am, that is, of how brief a span. Then חלד cheled also means the world, as in Ps. XLIX, 2. Hear, all ye inhabitants of חלד, the world: because the world and the things in it consist of a fixed duration. So also עולם olam, its synonym, first means age and eternity, and then also the world, as everyone knows.

In place of the true name of the mole, namely חולד choled, Levit. XI, 29., the interpreters substitute another: namely תנשמת thinsemeth in the following verse, which is rendered mole by Onkelos, the Greeks, Jerome, Jarchi, Kimchi, Pomarius, Pagninus, Arias, the Italians, the English, the Genevans, and nearly all the new versions there are. But although
Their number defends them, and phalanxes joined boss to boss,

I nevertheless see nothing certain in this rendering. Indeed, if חולד choled truly is the mole, which we consider now established, then תנשמת thinsemeth is something else. For in the list of creeping things rejected as unclean, Moses names these two separately, as different animals. And since there are eight in all, the first in that list is חולד choled and the last is תנשמת thinsemeth, so that they could not have been placed further apart from each other. But in the following book we shall show what תנשמת thinsemeth is.
